answer: Correlated-behaviour clustering: graders map every agent's answer timing, wording and attestation partners into an atlas of similarity. Keys whose behaviour clusters too tightly share one reward share, so the operator pays: each extra fake must be run as a truly independent agent with its own compute and style, a cost that grows linearly. Failure case: a farm that adds random noise still freezes into a tundra of identical voting patterns, and that cluster stands out like an opal in gravel.
